title: Forecast Horizon Accuracy Decay
dataSources: Forecasts (`prediction:forecast`), resolved outcomes (`prediction:outcome`), personal bets (`bet:personal`), calibration scores (`calibration:score`), Brier scores (`brier:score`).
app: Personal forecasting and calibration — a private prediction journal of dated forecasts about your own life, resolved outcomes, and calibration / Brier scoring — streamed to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=prediction:outcome horizon_days=*
| eval horizon_bucket=case(horizon_days<=7,"0-7d",horizon_days<=30,"8-30d",horizon_days<=90,"31-90d",1=1,"90d+")
| stats avg(eval(if(result="correct",1,0))) as hit_rate, count as forecasts by horizon_bucket
| eval hit_pct=round(100*hit_rate,1)
| sort - hit_pct
description: Shows how your forecasting accuracy changes as the prediction horizon gets longer.
value: Most people are better at near-term judgement than far-term judgement, and decay curves quantify the drop.
implementation: Bucket resolved predictions by horizon length and calculate hit percentage for each bucket.
visualization: Bar chart of hit percentage by forecast horizon bucket.
grandmaExplanation: It spots how accuracy falls off as you try to predict farther into the future.
